doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Dizzy, Bird and Thelonious Monk
summary: Mullins respects Dizzy and Bird, and calls Monk a genius whose tunes will last.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: What did you think of the late 40s and the early 50s with Dizzy and Charlie Parker and —
Oh, I respect those guys highly. Boy they were tremendous musicians, Dizzy and Bird. And they started something man. It was artistic. They started something. Yeah.
You like Monk? © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

I’ll tell you, at first, when I first heard him, I kind of stepped back, damn, man. Just like a lot of other people. But he was the master of his fate. He knew his music, and he played his music. I would call him a genius. I would go that far. There’s so many tunes that he composed man that were hell of a jazz tune, and they’ll be around a long time. They’ll be played a long time.
